title: Ha Mim again: the same Voice is speaking.
subtitle: A surah that continues the one before it
then: Ash-Shura seems to have come right after Fussilat, which also opened with Ha Mim. Fussilat confronted the Quraysh for their deaf opposition. This surah turns to patient teaching. {idea}The meaning of these letters is known to Allah.{/idea} They tell the listener: the same Voice is speaking again.
now: You hear a familiar ringtone and know who is calling before you look. {idea}These letters work a little like that.{/idea} Before the next words, take a breath and give them your full attention.
old: Letters I cannot explain are just a formality I can rush past.
new: The letters are a pause from Allah. Their meaning is with Him; my part is to attend.
try: Read the first five verses of this surah slowly today, out loud if you can.

title: Ayn Sin Qaf: a second pause before the message.
subtitle: Two sets of letters, double the attention
then: This surah opens with two sets of letters, a rare double opening. Ibn Kathir notes he has already discussed these letters elsewhere and moves on to the message. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah{/idea}, and the verse right after speaks of how revelation comes.
now: Someone says your name twice before saying something important. You look up. {idea}A second set of letters is a second call to look up.{/idea} You do not have to decode it. You just have to be present.
old: If I cannot understand a verse, it has nothing to give me.
new: Some verses teach by stopping me. Humility before what I do not know is part of reading.
try: Sit for one quiet minute before opening the Quran next time, with no phone in reach.

title: The same revelation came to messengers before you.
subtitle: Nothing strange about a message from God
then: The Quraysh were amazed that revelation came to a man. Ibn Kathir says {idea}just as this Quran came to you, Books came to the prophets before.{/idea} Aishah described seeing the Prophet ﷺ receiving revelation on a very cold day, with {idea}beads of sweat on his forehead{/idea} when it ended.
now: Your grandparents prayed the same prayer you pray. Their grandparents too, back and back. {idea}You are not trying something new.{/idea} You are joining a line that stretches to the first prophets.
old: Religion is something people made up along the way.
new: The same Wise God has been speaking to humanity through messengers from the start.
try: Learn the name of one earlier prophet you know little about and read a little of his story.

title: Everything in the heavens and earth is His.
subtitle: The Most High, the Most Great
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}everything is subject to His dominion and control.{/idea} He links the names Most High and Most Great to similar verses. The Quraysh treated idols as partners in ownership. This verse leaves no share for anyone else.
now: Your car, your flat, your savings, your time. You guard them like they are yours forever. {idea}Every one of them is His.{/idea} That can feel like loss, or like relief: you are a caretaker, not the final owner.
old: What I have is mine, and I have to protect it at all costs.
new: Everything belongs to the Most High. I am looking after things He lent me.
try: Lend or give one thing you own to someone today, remembering it was His first.

title: The heavens nearly split, and angels ask forgiveness for you.
subtitle: Awe above, mercy for those on earth
then: Ibn Abbas and others said the heavens nearly split {trap}out of fear of His might.{/trap} At the same moment the angels glorify Him and {reward}ask forgiveness for those on earth.{/reward} Ibn Kathir links it to the angels who carry the Throne praying for believers. Then: Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
now: You are stuck in traffic, annoyed, not thinking of Allah at all. {reward}Somewhere above you, angels are asking forgiveness for people on earth.{/reward} You are being prayed for while you are not praying.
old: No one is thinking about me or praying for me.
new: Angels ask forgiveness for those on earth. Allah's mercy surrounds me even when I forget Him.
try: Ask forgiveness today for someone else by name, the way the angels do for us.

title: Allah keeps watch over them; you are not their manager.
subtitle: Your job is to remind, not to control
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}is witness to their deeds, recording them precisely.{/idea} To the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}you are just a warner, and Allah is Trustee of all affairs.{/idea} The Quraysh's choices were not his burden to carry.
now: Your brother has stopped praying. You have tried every argument. You lie awake about it. {idea}You are not his manager.{/idea} Remind him kindly, make dua, and let Allah carry what only He can carry.
old: If someone I love goes astray, it means I failed them.
new: My role is to remind with care. Their hearts and their record are with Allah.
try: Make a sincere dua today for one person you worry about, then let the worry rest with Allah.

title: A clear Quran to warn Makkah and the world around it.
subtitle: The Day of Gathering, two groups
then: Ibn Kathir says Makkah was called the Mother of Towns because it is {idea}the most beloved land to Allah{/idea}, and the warning reached all lands. When companions asked why strive if all is written, the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}strive for the middle course, or close to it.{/idea}
now: You hear talk of destiny and think, if it is all written, what is the point. {idea}The Prophet's ﷺ answer is simple: keep working, stay balanced.{/idea} Your deeds today are how the end is reached.
old: If my end is already written, my effort does not change anything.
new: The Prophet ﷺ answered that worry with work. Strive steadily, and trust Allah with the end.
try: Pick one good deed you have been half-doing and do it fully today.

title: He could have made one nation; He admits whom He wills.
subtitle: Difference among people is part of His wisdom
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah could have made people {idea}all following guidance or all misguidance{/idea}, but He made them different, with complete wisdom and perfect proof. {reward}He admits whom He wills into His mercy.{/reward}
now: You see how differently people around you live: some pray, some never think of it. {reward}If you are on the path, it is His mercy that brought you in.{/reward} That is a reason for gratitude, not for looking down on anyone.
old: I found faith because I am smarter or better than others.
new: Being guided is a mercy Allah gave me. It should make me grateful and humble.
try: Thank Allah today, in your own words, for guiding you to whatever faith you have.

title: Other protectors? Allah alone is the Protector.
subtitle: The One who gives life to the dead
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}denounces the idolators for taking other gods{/trap} and declares He alone is the true God. {idea}He brings the dead back to life and is able to do all things.{/idea} No idol in Makkah could protect anyone.
now: You count on the right contact at work, the friend who knows a lawyer, the backup plan. {trap}They help, but they are not protection.{/trap} {idea}The One who gives life is the one who truly protects.{/idea}
old: My real protection is the people and plans I have in place.
new: People and plans are means. Allah alone is the Protector behind them all.
try: Before your next big task today, say hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: Whatever you disagree on, the judgment is Allah's.
subtitle: Trust Him and turn back to Him
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}general and applies to all things{/idea}: He is the Judge according to His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. Then the Prophet ﷺ says: {reward}in Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn.{/reward}
now: The family group chat is heating up. Everyone has an opinion and nobody is listening. {idea}Some arguments are not mine to win.{/idea} The verse invites you to step back, refer it to Allah, and trust Him.
old: I need to win this argument to be at peace.
new: The final judgment is Allah's. I can say my piece, then trust Him with the rest.
try: In your next disagreement, stop after one calm reply and say, Allah knows best.

title: There is nothing like Him.
subtitle: The Maker of pairs has no pair
then: Ibn Kathir says He made your kind male and female {reward}as a blessing and a favor{/reward}, generation after generation. Yet {idea}there is nothing like the Creator of these pairs; He is unique, with no peer or equal.{/idea} And He hears and sees all.
now: You picture Allah like a stern teacher, or a distant boss, or a disappointed parent. {idea}Every picture falls short.{/idea} He is not like anyone you know, and still He hears your whisper and sees your tears.
old: I imagine Allah like a person I know, just bigger.
new: Nothing is like Him, yet He hears and sees me completely.
try: Say a dua today aloud, knowing the All-Hearer hears every word.

title: He holds the keys, and measures out provision.
subtitle: More for some, less for others, all with knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir says the keys mean {idea}He is the One controlling and governing them.{/idea} He gives plenty to some and less to others, and He is {idea}perfectly Wise and Just{/idea}, knowing all things.
now: Your friend's salary is double yours. Your sibling just bought a house. You check your bank app and feel small. {idea}The One with the keys measured both shares, knowing what each of you needs.{/idea}
old: If I have less than others, Allah must be less pleased with me.
new: Provision is measured with wisdom and knowledge. More or less is not a verdict on my worth.
try: Thank Allah for one thing you have today without comparing it to anyone.

title: One religion from Nuh to Muhammad ﷺ: establish it, do not split.
subtitle: The shared message of the great messengers
then: Ibn Kathir notes this verse names the first messenger after Adam, Nuh, the last, Muhammad ﷺ, and the strong-willed ones between. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}we prophets are brothers and our religion is one.{/idea} All were told to {idea}establish religion and not divide in it.{/idea}
now: A small difference in practice becomes a heated thread. Friends stop speaking over it. {trap}Division grows from small things.{/trap} {idea}The verse reminds you of the one message all the prophets shared.{/idea}
old: Proving I am right about small details is defending the faith.
new: The prophets shared one religion and were told not to split. Unity is part of establishing it.
try: Reach out to one person you have drifted from over a religious disagreement, and just say salam.

title: They split after knowledge came, out of rivalry.
subtitle: Division is rarely about lack of knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}their opposition arose after the truth had come{/trap} and proof was established. Only transgression and stubbornness made them split. The generations after them {trap}merely imitated their forefathers, without evidence{/trap}, and were left confused and doubtful.
now: Two cousins stop speaking for years over an inheritance. Both know what is fair. {trap}It is not a knowledge problem. It is a pride problem.{/trap} And their children grow up repeating the feud without knowing why.
old: We fell out because we just see things differently.
new: Often we split not from ignorance but from ego. And our children inherit what we leave unresolved.
try: Think of one quarrel you inherited from your family and ask whether it is really yours to keep.

title: Invite, stand firm, be just, and let Allah gather us.
subtitle: A verse of ten instructions
then: Scholars said this verse holds {idea}ten separate ideas{/idea}, like Ayat al-Kursi. The Prophet ﷺ was told to invite, stand firm, not follow their desires, believe in all revealed Books, and {idea}do justice among them.{/idea} Mujahid said no dispute here meant no argument. {reward}Allah will gather us all.{/reward}
now: At work you are the only one who does not join in the after-hours drinks. You do not lecture, you do not cave. {idea}You stay firm, fair to everyone, and calm.{/idea} The verse is a full plan for living among people who differ from you.
old: Standing by my faith means either blending in or arguing.
new: I can stay firm, treat everyone justly, skip the argument, and leave the final word to Allah.
try: Be noticeably fair today to someone who does not share your beliefs.

title: Arguing people out of faith they already answered.
subtitle: Such arguments fall flat with their Lord
then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said they {trap}argued with the believers after they had responded to Allah, hoping to pull them back{/trap} to the old ways. Ibn Kathir calls the argument futile before Allah. The new Muslims in Makkah faced this every day.
now: You started praying again. An old friend sends long messages about why it is pointless. {trap}It shakes you.{/trap} {idea}You do not have to win the debate to keep your prayer.{/idea} Their argument does not weigh anything with Allah.
old: If I cannot answer every objection, maybe my faith is weak.
new: Arguments meant to pull me away carry no weight with Allah. I can keep walking.
try: If someone pressures you about your faith this week, answer kindly once, then let it go.

title: The Book and the Balance, and maybe the Hour is near.
subtitle: Truth to follow, justice to keep
then: Mujahid and Qatadah said the Balance means {idea}justice and fairness.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the line about the Hour is {idea}encouragement to strive for it, a warning, and advice to think little of this world.{/idea}
now: You measure carefully when you are owed: the bill split, the hours worked. Less carefully when you owe. {idea}The Balance is for both sides.{/idea} And perhaps the Hour is closer than your next payday.
old: I will start being careful about fairness when life slows down.
new: Allah sent truth and a Balance. The Hour may be near, so fairness cannot wait.
try: Settle one small thing you owe someone today, even a borrowed item.

title: Deniers rush the Hour; believers prepare for it.
subtitle: What have you prepared for it
then: A man called out to the Prophet ﷺ on a journey: when will the Hour come? He replied, {idea}it will surely come. What have you prepared for it?{/idea} The man said, love of Allah and His Messenger. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}you will be with those you love.{/reward}
now: You watch a video predicting the end of the world and scroll on. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ turned the question around.{/idea} Not when, but what are you bringing. {reward}Even love counts.{/reward}
old: The big question about the Hour is when it will happen.
new: The real question is what I am preparing. Love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is a start.
try: Do one act today purely out of love for Allah, and name it to yourself as preparation.

title: Allah is gentle with His servants and forgets no one.
subtitle: Provision for the righteous and the sinner
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}provides for every last one of them and does not forget anyone.{/reward} When it comes to provision, {idea}the righteous and the sinner are alike.{/idea} He links it to the verse that every creature on earth has its provision from Allah.
now: You had a week where you barely prayed. Still the salary came, still the fridge had food, still you woke up. {reward}His kindness did not wait for you to deserve it.{/reward}
old: Allah only provides for me when I am doing well.
new: Allah's gentleness reaches every creature. He has not forgotten me on my worst day.
try: Open your fridge today and thank Allah for one item in it.

title: Plant for the Hereafter and He grows your harvest.
subtitle: Two fields, two harvests
then: Ibn Kathir says whoever works for the Hereafter, Allah {reward}helps him and multiplies every good from ten to seven hundred times.{/reward} Whoever works only for this world may or may not get it, and {trap}has the worst deal in both.{/trap} A hadith warns against doing deeds of the Hereafter for worldly gain.
now: You are working long hours for a promotion. Nothing wrong with that. {idea}The question is what the field is for.{/idea} The same job, done honestly and to feed your family for Allah's sake, becomes a Hereafter harvest.
old: Work is for this world, and worship is for the next.
new: The same effort can be planted for the Hereafter if I intend it, and then He grows it.
try: Before work tomorrow, make a quiet intention that it is for Allah and your family.

title: Who gave them a religion Allah never allowed?
subtitle: Rules people invent and call religion
then: Ibn Kathir says in the time of ignorance people {trap}invented taboos on animals and false rulings on permitted and forbidden{/trap}, and false rites of worship. He names Amr bin Luhayy as the one who first brought idol worship to Quraysh. A decisive word delayed their judgment.
now: Your family insists something is part of religion. You look, and it is just old custom. Or you skip something real because it is inconvenient. {idea}Religion is what Allah sent, not what we add or drop.{/idea}
old: If my family always did it this way, it must be religion.
new: Only Allah ordains religion. Customs are fine as customs, but not as His command.
try: Pick one practice you assume is religious and look up its source this week.

title: Fearful of what they earned, or in flowering meadows.
subtitle: The great bounty for those who believe and do good

key.label: What we fear on that Day

then: Ibn Kathir paints the contrast: one standing in fear {trap}of what they earned{/trap}, another in the gardens enjoying {reward}what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no mind has imagined.{/reward} He calls it the ultimate victory and complete blessing.
now: You lie awake replaying something you said at work. The fear is of your own words. {idea}The verse says the Day will feel like that, or like the opposite.{/idea} Today's deeds decide which.
old: What I fear most is what others might do to me.
new: On that Day the only thing to fear is my own record. I can fill it with good today.
try: Do one deed today that you would be glad to meet again on the Day.

title: No payment asked, only that you honor the ties between us.
subtitle: And every good deed is increased
then: Ibn Abbas explained there was {idea}no clan of Quraysh the Prophet ﷺ was not related to.{/idea} He asked only that they uphold the kinship and let him convey the message without harm. Then the promise: {reward}whoever does good, We increase it.{/reward} Allah forgives much and multiplies a little.
now: You do a small favor for a cousin you barely talk to. It feels like nothing. {reward}Allah is Shakur: He appreciates and increases the small.{/reward} And kinship itself is something the Prophet ﷺ asked people to honor.
old: Small good deeds do not really add up to much.
new: Allah is Appreciative. He takes my small good and increases it.
try: Send a kind message today to a relative you have not spoken to in a while.

title: He made it up? Allah could have sealed his heart.
subtitle: Falsehood is erased, truth established
then: Some said the Prophet ﷺ had invented a lie about Allah. Ibn Kathir explains: if he had, {idea}Allah could have sealed his heart and made him forget what had come to him.{/idea} Instead, {reward}Allah wipes out falsehood and establishes the truth by His words.{/reward} He knows what is in every heart.
now: Someone spreads a false story about you at work. It hurts, and you want to answer every word. {reward}Truth has a way of standing up over time.{/reward} {idea}Allah knows what is in every chest, including theirs and yours.{/idea}
old: If a lie spreads far enough, it becomes the truth.
new: Allah erases falsehood and makes truth firm. He knows every heart.
try: If someone has wronged you with words, make dua for the truth to be clear instead of replying.

title: He accepts repentance, pardons, and knows what you did.
subtitle: Allah's joy at a servant coming back

key.label: What He does with the past

then: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is {reward}more pleased with His servant's repentance{/reward} than a man who lost his camel with his food and water in the desert, gave up, lay down to die, then found it standing beside him. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}He knows all your deeds, yet still accepts repentance.{/idea}
now: You have been away a long time. You think you need to clean yourself up before you can come back. {reward}He already knows everything, and still waits to be glad you returned.{/reward}
old: Allah knows how bad I have been, so He must be done with me.
new: He knows everything I did and still accepts me back, more joyful than a man who found his lost camel.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one specific thing, then believe He accepted it.

title: He answers those who believe and gives them more.
subtitle: Duas answered, with extra besides
then: Ibn Jarir said He {reward}answers their supplication for themselves, their companions and their brothers.{/reward} An-Nakha'i said they intercede for their brothers, and then for their brothers' brothers. The verse balances this with a warning for those who disbelieve.
now: You whisper a dua for your friend going through a divorce, then one for her sister you have never met. {reward}The verse says those duas are answered and more is added.{/reward} Your prayers can reach people you will never meet.
old: My duas are small and probably do not reach far.
new: Allah answers the believers and adds from His bounty, even for the people they pray for.
try: Make dua today for a friend, and for someone dear to that friend.

title: Too much provision would make us tyrants, so He measures it.
subtitle: Why you do not have more

key.label: Why I have what I have

then: Ibn Kathir says if He gave people {trap}more provision than they need, it would make them rebel and transgress{/trap} against one another arrogantly. Instead {idea}He gives provision according to what is in their best interests{/idea}, and He knows best.
now: You imagine winning the lottery: the house, the car, finally free. {trap}Then you think of the people you know who got rich and changed.{/trap} {idea}What you have may be exactly what keeps your heart soft.{/idea}
old: If I just had a lot more money, I would be a better person.
new: Allah measures my provision knowing my heart. Sometimes less is His protection.
try: Next time you wish for more, add a dua: give me what is good for my heart.

title: Rain comes after people have given up.
subtitle: Mercy arrives at the edge of despair
then: Ibn Kathir says He sends rain {reward}after people have given up hope, at their time of need.{/reward} A man told Umar there was no rain and people were in despair. Umar said, {reward}rain will be sent upon you{/reward}, and recited this verse.
now: Months of job applications. Months of trying for a child. Months waiting for a diagnosis to change. {trap}You stopped expecting anything.{/trap} {reward}This verse is about the rain that comes right then.{/reward}
old: I have waited so long that nothing is going to change now.
new: Allah often sends His rain after people have given up. Despair is not the end of the story.
try: Make one dua today for the thing you stopped asking for.

title: Every creature scattered in the heavens and earth, gathered by Him.
subtitle: The variety of life, and the Day of gathering
then: Ibn Kathir says these creatures include {idea}angels, men, jinn and all animals, with different shapes, colors, languages and natures{/idea}, spread through every region. Yet He will {idea}gather the first and last of them in one place{/idea} and judge with justice.
now: You stand in a crowded train station: hundreds of faces, languages, stories. Pigeons on the roof, ants on the floor. {idea}He made every one and will gather every one.{/idea} Not one is lost in the crowd, including you.
old: In a world this big, I am just one face lost in the crowd.
new: Allah spread every creature across the earth and will gather each one. I am not lost to Him.
try: In the next crowd you are in, look around and say subhanallah once.

title: Hardship from what our hands earned, and He pardons much.
subtitle: Even a thorn can wipe away a sin
then: Ibn Kathir says misfortunes come from past sins, but {reward}He pardons much and does not punish for most.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}no believer is struck by fatigue, worry or grief, even a thorn, but Allah forgives some of his sins by it.{/reward}
now: You stub your toe, miss the bus, get a headache before a long shift. Small, annoying things. {reward}For a believer, none of it is wasted.{/reward} And the verse turns you gently to your own conduct, not anyone else's.
old: When bad things happen, Allah must be angry with me.
new: Hardship can be a cleansing, and Allah pardons far more than He ever holds against me.
try: When something small goes wrong today, say alhamdulillah and ask Allah to make it expiation.

title: Nowhere on earth to escape Him, no helper besides Him.
subtitle: The only protector is the One you would run from
then: This follows the verse about misfortune and pardon. The listeners in Makkah were told: {idea}you cannot escape Allah anywhere on earth{/idea}, and {idea}besides Him you have no protector or helper.{/idea} The way out of hardship is toward Him.
now: You moved cities, changed jobs, deleted the old number. The guilt came with you. {idea}There is nowhere to run from Allah.{/idea} {reward}But you can always run to Him.{/reward}
old: If I put enough distance between me and my past, it will go away.
new: I cannot escape Allah, and I do not need to. He is the only helper I can run to.
try: Instead of avoiding a heavy feeling today, sit with it for a minute and hand it to Allah in dua.

title: Ships on the sea like mountains: a sign.
subtitle: The ocean made to carry you
then: Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others said these ships sail the sea {idea}like mountains on land.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it is a sign of His power that {idea}He subjugated the sea so ships may sail in it by His command.{/idea}
now: You see a container ship on the horizon, or track a parcel crossing an ocean. Your phone, your shoes, your food all floated here. {idea}Mountains on the water, held up by His command.{/idea}
old: Huge ships and global shipping are just human achievement.
new: Behind every vessel crossing the sea is the One who made the sea carry it.
try: Pick one thing you own that came from overseas and thank Allah for the journey it made.

title: If He stilled the wind, the ships would stop.
subtitle: Signs for the patient and the grateful
then: Ibn Kathir says if He willed, the winds would stop and ships would stay {trap}still on the water, neither coming nor going.{/trap} The signs are for {idea}everyone patient in difficulty and grateful in ease.{/idea}
now: A power cut. The Wi-Fi drops. The train stops between stations and nobody moves. {trap}Everything you depend on can freeze in a moment.{/trap} {idea}Patience when it stops, gratitude when it runs.{/idea}
old: The systems I depend on will just keep working.
new: Everything keeps moving only by His will. Patience and gratitude help me see it.
try: When something you rely on works smoothly today, say alhamdulillah for it.

title: He could wreck them for their deeds, but pardons much.
subtitle: Wind in just the right amount
then: Ibn Kathir says if He punished for all sins, {trap}He would destroy everyone who sails.{/trap} Instead, {reward}by His grace He sends the wind according to their needs{/reward}, like rain that is just sufficient: too much would wreck houses, too little would starve crops.
now: Your life has a hundred moving parts that could each go wrong today. Most do not. {reward}Not because you deserve it, but because He pardons much{/reward} and sends just enough.
old: My life runs smoothly because I manage it well.
new: So much is held in balance for me, not because I earned it, but because He pardons much.
try: Tonight, list three things that could have gone wrong today but did not, and thank Him.

title: Those who argue against His signs have no way out.
subtitle: The sea itself answers the argument
then: After the signs of the sea, Ibn Kathir says those who dispute them {trap}have no means of escape, for they are subdued by His power.{/trap} The people of Makkah were traders who knew the sea and the wind. The sign was close to their own lives.
now: You can argue about anything online until 2am. {idea}But a sign is not there to win a debate.{/idea} It is there to change how you live. Which sign in your life have you only argued about?
old: As long as I can argue a point, I do not have to act on it.
new: Signs are meant to be heeded, not debated. Arguing does not give me a way out.
try: Skip one online argument today and use the time for a quiet dhikr instead.

title: What you have is for now; what is with Allah lasts.
subtitle: The start of a portrait of believers
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}no matter what you achieve and amass, do not be deceived by it{/trap}; it will end. {reward}What is with Allah is better and lasts forever.{/reward} It is for believers who are patient and rely on their Lord. This begins a list of qualities.
now: The new phone is old in a year. The car loses value the day you drive it out. The holiday photos are already buried in your gallery. {reward}Some things do not depreciate.{/reward}
old: Getting more now is how I secure a good life.
new: What I have now is brief enjoyment. What Allah keeps for me is better and lasting.
try: Before your next purchase, pause and give a small amount in charity first.

title: They avoid the major sins, and when angry, they forgive.
subtitle: Anger that ends in forgiveness
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}their nature is to forgive and be tolerant; vengeance is not in their nature.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ {reward}never took revenge for his own sake{/reward}, only when the sacred limits of Allah were violated.
now: Your spouse says something sharp in front of the kids. You feel the heat rise. {idea}The verse does not say they never get angry.{/idea} It says the anger ends in forgiveness instead of a scorecard.
old: If I forgive too quickly, I am letting people off too easily.
new: Believers get angry too, but they choose to forgive. That is strength, not weakness.
try: Forgive one small hurt from this week, out loud or in your heart, before you sleep.

title: They answer their Lord, pray, consult, and give.
subtitle: The verse that names the surah
then: This verse gives the surah its name, Ash-Shura, consultation. Ibn Kathir says {idea}they make no decision without consulting one another.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ consulted his companions so they would feel confident. Spending means {reward}treating people kindly, starting with those closest.{/reward}
now: A big family decision: moving, a school, caring for a parent. You could decide alone and announce it. {idea}Or you could sit everyone down and ask.{/idea} The verse puts consultation right next to prayer.
old: Asking others for input makes me look weak or unsure.
new: Believers decide together. Consultation sits beside prayer and giving as a mark of faith.
try: Ask someone close to you for their opinion on a decision you are facing this week.

title: Not helpless when wronged, yet choosing to forgive.
subtitle: Strength that is able to defend
then: Ibn Kathir says they {idea}are not incapable or helpless{/idea}, yet when able to respond they often prefer to forgive. Yusuf told his brothers {reward}no blame on you today{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ forgave a man who drew a sword on him while he slept.
now: You have the screenshot that would embarrass the person who wronged you. One tap and it is out. {idea}You are not helpless.{/idea} {reward}Choosing not to tap, from strength, is what this verse admires.{/reward}
old: Forgiving means letting people walk over me.
new: Believers can stand up for themselves, and their forgiveness comes from strength.
try: Delete one thing you were holding onto to use against someone.

title: Justice allows the like; forgiveness earns reward from Allah.
subtitle: Forgiving never lowers you
then: Ibn Kathir says justice is allowed, but {idea}the better way, forgiving, is recommended.{/idea} Whoever pardons and reconciles, {reward}his reward is with Allah and will not be wasted.{/reward} A hadith says {reward}Allah only increases the one who forgives in honor.{/reward} He does not love those who start the harm.
now: Your friend lets you down badly. Fair would be to drop them the way they dropped you. {reward}Better is to pardon and repair.{/reward} You worry you will look like a pushover. Allah says it raises you.
old: If I forgive and make peace, people will respect me less.
new: Fairness is allowed, but forgiveness and reconciliation bring reward from Allah and honor.
try: Take one step today toward mending a relationship where you were the one wronged.

title: Standing up for yourself after a wrong is not a sin.
subtitle: The wronged person is not the one blamed
then: These verses come right after the description of believers who consult each other and defend themselves when wronged. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}there is no sin on the one who answers back{/idea} against the person who wronged him. The burden sits on whoever started it, as long as the reply does not go too far.
now: A coworker takes credit for your report in front of the manager. You calmly send the email with the original timestamps. Part of you feels guilty, as if a good person would just swallow it. {idea}A fair answer is not a sin.{/idea} {trap}Going past fair is.{/trap}
old: If I defend myself, I am being as bad as them.
new: A measured response to a real wrong carries no blame. Only the starter and the one who oversteps are blamed.
try: Think of one wrong you swallowed out of guilt. Decide on one calm, fair sentence you could say about it.

title: The blame falls on the one who oppresses first.
subtitle: Starting harm is what gets held to account

picture.label: Where the path of blame runs

then: Ibn Kathir quotes a Sahih hadith: when two people insult each other, {trap}the one who began carries the blame{/trap}, unless the wronged one goes too far. He also tells of a governor who was advised to sleep only after making sure his hands held no one's blood or wealth unjustly.
now: In the family group chat an old argument flares up. Someone says "you are both as bad as each other." Maybe. Or maybe one person lit the match. {idea}Ask yourself honestly which one you are.{/idea}
old: In any conflict, everyone shares the blame equally.
new: Allah sees who started the harm, and that is where the weight falls.
try: Before sleeping tonight, check one thing: do you owe anyone an apology or a debt? Settle one.

title: Patience and forgiving take more strength than revenge.
subtitle: The harder, higher choice after being wronged
then: Having allowed a fair reply, the passage now points higher. Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}bearing the insult with patience and covering the wrong{/idea}. He cites a Sahih hadith: Allah does not increase a person who forgives except in {reward}honor{/reward}.
now: Your sibling said something cruel at a family dinner years ago. You have every right to bring it up. Instead you choose, on purpose, to let it go and still call on their birthday. {idea}That is not weakness. It takes real strength.{/idea}
old: If I forgive, I lose and they win.
new: Forgiving is the strong choice, and Allah raises the one who makes it.
try: Pick one small hurt from this week and forgive it fully. Do not mention it again.

title: Is there any way back? The question that comes too late.
subtitle: Wishing for a second chance after time runs out
then: The Makkan listeners were told how the wrongdoers will react on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will wish they could go back to this world{/trap}, and links it to another passage where they say, if only we were sent back.
now: You keep a list in your head: pray properly from next month, call your mother more once work calms down. The list never shrinks. {idea}The "way back" they will beg for is the day you are living now.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of time to turn things around.
new: The return people will long for later is open to me today.
try: Take one item off your someday list and do it today, even a small piece of it.

title: The real losers are those who lose themselves and family.
subtitle: What true loss looks like on the final Day
then: The scene shows people brought before the Fire, {trap}humbled, stealing glances{/trap} out of fear. Ibn Kathir explains that the believers will name them the greatest losers: they lose themselves and are {trap}separated from their families and companions{/trap}.
now: You lose a deal and cannot sleep. You check the stock app ten times a day. Meanwhile your kids eat dinner while you scroll. {idea}This verse redraws the map of what losing really means.{/idea}
old: Real loss is about money, career, and reputation.
new: The loss that matters is losing my own soul and the bond with the people I love.
try: Tonight, put the phone in another room for one meal and be fully with your family.

title: No helper other than Allah will stand for them.
subtitle: Every backup besides Allah falls away
then: The Quraysh leaned on tribe, alliances and idols. Ibn Kathir explains that on that Day {trap}no one will save them from what they face{/trap}, and whoever Allah lets go astray has {trap}no way to salvation{/trap}.
now: You know a person in every office. A cousin in HR, a friend at the bank. It feels like a safety net for anything. {idea}Connections help here, but they are not who you will stand with on the last Day.{/idea}
old: As long as I have the right people, I am covered.
new: Every helper but Allah eventually steps back. My real backing is my relationship with Him.
try: Next time you reach for a contact to solve a problem, make a short dua first.

title: Answer your Lord before the Day no one can push back.
subtitle: An invitation with a deadline

row.title: refuge from Him is with Him

then: After describing the Day, the verse turns to the listeners with a direct call. Ibn Kathir says once Allah commands it, {trap}it comes in the blink of an eye{/trap}, and there is no place to hide, and {reward}no refuge from Him except with Him{/reward}.
now: The notification says "Your session will expire in 60 seconds." You rush to save. Life has a timer too, without the countdown on screen. {idea}This verse is the gentle notification.{/idea}
old: I will respond when I am ready.
new: The call is open now, and the only safe place from Allah is running toward Him.
try: Answer one call of Allah today right away: pray the next prayer at its start time.

title: Your job is to deliver. Hearts belong to Allah.
subtitle: The messenger's limit, and the human mood swing

row.title: today is everything
sub: ease, I boast; pain, I despair

then: The Prophet ﷺ was told that if the idolaters turned away, {idea}his duty was only to convey{/idea}. Then the verse describes people: Ibn Kathir says in hardship a person {trap}forgets the previous times of ease{/trap} and sees only the present. He cites the hadith that the believer thanks in good times and is patient in bad, and both are good for him.
now: You shared a reminder with a friend and they ignored it. You feel like you failed. Then a bad week at work, and you say "nothing ever goes right for me," forgetting last month's raise. {idea}Deliver, then let go. Remember the good.{/idea}
old: If they do not change, I failed; if today is bad, life is bad.
new: My part is to deliver kindly. And one hard day does not erase years of blessings.
try: Write down three good things from the past month that you have stopped noticing.

title: Daughters or sons: each child is a gift He chooses.
subtitle: Children come by His will, not our design
then: The surah closes by reminding the Makkans who rules creation. Ibn Kathir notes some are given {reward}daughters only{/reward}, as Al-Baghawi said of Lut, and some {reward}sons only{/reward}, as of Ibrahim. Both are described with the same word: a gift.
now: At the baby shower, an aunt says "next time, insha'Allah, a boy." Or the reverse. The parents smile politely. {idea}The verse uses one word for both: He grants.{/idea} Neither is the consolation prize.
old: Having a certain kind of child would make the family complete.
new: Every child is a deliberate gift from the Owner of everything.
try: Tell a parent you know, sincerely, that their child is a gift. Mean it for whatever child they have.

title: Some get both, some get none. He knows why.
subtitle: Childlessness is also within His wise knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir lists four groups of people: given daughters, given sons, given both, and given none. Al-Baghawi names {idea}Yahya and Isa{/idea} among those who had no children, noble prophets. The verse ends: {idea}He is Knowing and Able{/idea}.
now: Another wedding, another relative asking "any news yet?" You smile and change the subject, then cry in the car. {idea}The verse places you in the same company as prophets{/idea}, inside His knowledge, not outside His care.
old: Not having children means I am lacking or being punished.
new: Whether I have children or not, it is known and chosen by the All-Knowing.
try: If someone you know is waiting for a child, do not ask "any news?" Pray for them quietly instead.

title: How Allah speaks to a human: three ways only.
subtitle: Revelation, behind a veil, or through a messenger
then: The Makkans were amazed that a man could receive revelation. Ibn Kathir explains the three ways: something {idea}cast into the heart{/idea} of the Prophet ﷺ, speech {idea}from behind a veil{/idea} as with Musa, or an angel like Jibril sent with the message.
now: You wish for a sign, a dream, a voice telling you what to do about the job offer. Meanwhile the Quran sits on your shelf, the words He already sent through a messenger. {idea}He has spoken. The question is whether you open it.{/idea}
old: If Allah wanted to guide me, He would give me a clear sign.
new: He already speaks through what He sent. I need to listen to it.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page slowly, as if it was addressed to you.

title: He did not know the Book. Then came the light.
subtitle: The Quran as a spirit and a light
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the spirit of Our command means {idea}the Quran{/idea}. Before it, the Prophet ﷺ did not know the details of the Book or faith. Allah made it {reward}a light{/reward} to guide whom He wills, and he ﷺ guides to the straight path.
now: You walk into a dark room at night and fumble for the switch, banging your knee on the table. Then the light comes on and everything has a place. {reward}That is what this verse calls the Quran.{/reward}
old: The Quran is a book of rules I should read sometimes.
new: The Quran is a light sent to show me the straight path.
try: Pick one verse you read today and ask: what does this light show me in my own life?

title: All matters end up with Allah.
subtitle: The path belongs to the One who owns all
then: The surah ends here. Ibn Kathir says the path is {idea}His laws which He enjoins{/idea}, and He is the Lord and Sovereign of all. {idea}All matters come back to Him{/idea} and He judges them.
now: You are waiting on a visa decision, a test result, a court date. It feels like a stranger behind a desk holds your future. {idea}Every file ends up on His desk.{/idea}
old: My future depends on the people making decisions about me.
new: Every decision, every case, ends with Allah, who owns it all.
try: Name one outcome you are anxious about. Say: "to You all matters return," and hand it over.
